howTo.count-5: Count the pictures, then tap the number that tells how many.
howTo.count-10: Count the pictures one by one, then tap how many there are.
howTo.shapes: Listen for the shape, then tap it.
howTo.more-less: Look at both groups and tap the one with more.
howTo.quick-look-5: The dots only show for a moment. Look fast, then tap how many you saw.
howTo.quick-look-10: The dots only show for a moment. Look at the ten frame, then tap how many.
howTo.next-number: Look at the stairs. Are the numbers going up or down? Tap the number that comes next.
howTo.skip-count: The numbers jump by the same amount each time. Find the jump, then tap what comes next.
howTo.number-line-10: Tap the line where the number belongs. 0 is at the start and the end is the biggest.
howTo.number-line-100: Tap the line where the number belongs. Halfway is 50.
howTo.number-line-1000: Tap the line where the number belongs. Halfway is 500.
howTo.add-10: Put the two groups together and count them all.
howTo.sub-10: Start with the first number and take some away. How many are left?
howTo.sub-20: Take the second number away from the first.
howTo.add-100: Add the tens, then add the ones.
howTo.sub-100: Take away the tens, then take away the ones.
howTo.mult-2-5-10: Times means groups of. 3 × 5 is three groups of five.
howTo.mult-10: Times means groups of. Use the facts you know.
howTo.div-10: Divide means share equally. How many in each group?
howTo.mult-12: Use the times tables you know to build the big ones.
howTo.div-12: Think of the times fact that goes with it.
howTo.rhymes: Rhyming words end with the same sound, like cat and hat. Tap the one that rhymes.
howTo.sound-snack: Listen to the sound. Feed the monster the picture that starts with it.
howTo.letter-sounds: Listen to the sound, then tap the letter that makes it.
howTo.sight-words: Listen to the word, then tap it.
howTo.word-builder: Tap the letters in order to spell the word. Each letter says its sound.
howTo.digraph-starts: Two letters can make one sound, like sh in ship. Tap the sound the word starts with.
howTo.digraph-builder: Some tiles have two letters that make one sound. Spell the word with them.
howTo.story-strip: Tap the pictures in the order they happen: first, then next, then last.
howTo.word-parts: Find the part added to the word, like un or re, and what it means.
howTo.compound-words: A compound word is two words stuck together. Find where it splits.
howTo.dress-weather: Look at the weather, then pick what you need.
howTo.animal-homes: Where does this animal live? Tap its home.
howTo.plant-needs: Plants need some things to grow. Tap the one a plant needs.
howTo.push-pull: A push moves something away from you. A pull brings it closer.
howTo.life-cycles: Tap the pictures in order, from the start of life to grown up.
howTo.states-of-matter: Solids keep their shape, liquids pour, and gases float around.
howTo.food-chains: Energy starts with the sun. Tap who gets eaten first, up to the top hunter.
howTo.human-body: Think about what each part of your body does.
howTo.patterns-ab: Say the pattern out loud: red, blue, red, blue. Then tap what goes in the empty box.
howTo.patterns-easy: Find the part that repeats, then tap what goes in the empty box.
howTo.patterns-hard: Find the part that repeats. It can be longer this time!
howTo.pattern-match: Say the pattern with letters: A A B, A A B. Find the row that goes the same way with new things.
howTo.pattern-unit: Look for the smallest part that repeats again and again from the start.
howTo.growing-patterns: Each step grows by the same amount. Find how much it grows, then add it on.
howTo.pattern-position: Find how long the repeating part is. Jump that many at a time to reach the number.
howTo.number-rules: Look at how each number changes to get the next one. The change can grow or switch!
howTo.logic-grids: Read every clue. Each friend has a different pet.
howTo.feelings-faces: Look at the faces. Listen for the feeling, then tap the face that shows it.
howTo.feelings-situations: Think about how it would feel if this happened to you. Tap that face.
howTo.fair-play: Fair means everyone gets a chance. Tap the fair thing to do.
howTo.in-their-shoes: Imagine you are the person in the story. How would you feel, or what would help?

coach.intro: Sit together. Let your child tap the answers, and after each one use the prompt to talk about it.

right: Ask: "How did you work it out?"
Ask: "Can you show me with your fingers?"
Ask: "Is there another way to get the same answer?"
wrong: Work it out together, out loud. Count or draw it.
Ask: "Which part was tricky?" Then try it together.
Point at the right answer and say why it fits.

right: Ask: "Can you think of another word like that?"
Ask: "What sound does it start with?"
wrong: Say both words slowly and listen for the difference.
Ask: "What did you hear?" Then listen again with 🔊.

right: Ask: "Where have you seen that in real life?"
Ask: "Why do you think that's true?"
Look for one around you right now.
wrong: Read the explanation together and talk about it.
Ask: "What made you pick that?" Then look at the right answer.
Ask: "What do you already know about this?"

right: Make your own pattern for each other to guess.
wrong: Say the pattern out loud together until it repeats.
Point to each piece in turn and say it.

right: Ask: "Has something like this happened to you?"
Ask: "Why is that a kind choice?"
wrong: Ask: "How would the other person feel?"
Talk about why the right answer is kinder.
Act it out together: what would you say or do?
